draft.title: Biomes and food production
card: Crops need fertile soil, reliable rain and a growing season that is warm enough. Biomes that have these conditions are the best places to grow food.
Many temperate grasslands and temperate forests have these conditions. Much of the world's grain, such as wheat and maize, is grown in these biomes.
Because the land grows crops so well, much of it has been cleared of its natural plants and changed into farmland. Few areas of these biomes are still close to their natural state.
Biomes with poor soil, very little rain or a very cold climate, such as deserts and tundra, grow much less food.
draft.remember: Fertile soil and reliable rain make a biome good for farming, and many such biomes have been cleared for crops.

a.q: Why have so many temperate grasslands been turned into farmland?
opts: Their fertile soils and reliable rain suit crops
Their cold climate stops crops from growing
Their soils are poor, so farmers must replace them
Their rainfall is too low for any natural plants
a.why: Fertile soil and reliable rain are what crops need, so farmers cleared these grasslands to grow grain. The cold, poor soil and low rainfall in the other options would make farming harder, not easier.
a.clue: Think about what crops need to grow well.

b.q: Which place would be best for growing a large wheat crop?
opts: A temperate grassland with fertile soil and steady rain
A hot desert with sandy soil and very little rain
A tundra region with frozen ground for most of the year
A tropical rainforest with thin soil under dense trees
b.why: A temperate grassland with fertile soil and steady rain gives wheat what it needs. The desert has too little water and the tundra is too cold. A rainforest is warm and wet, but the card names it as neither a main grain biome nor one with fertile soil.
b.clue: Look for fertile soil and reliable rain together.

a.best: Their fertile soils and reliable rain suit crops

b.best: A temperate grassland with fertile soil and steady rain

problems.detail: The clue 'Look for fertile soil and reliable rain together' gives the answer away. Only one option names both, using nearly the same words, so a student can match the phrase without understanding the idea.

The why says 'the card names it [rainforest] as neither a main grain biome nor one with fertile soil', but the card never mentions rainforest. The reason it is a poor choice comes from the option's own 'thin soil', not from the card.

check.summary: Both answers are correct and the card is accurate. However, question b's clue gives away the answer by quoting the right option's wording, and its why wrongly says the card discusses rainforest.

proposal.title: Biomes and food production
card: Crops need fertile soil, reliable rain and a growing season that is warm enough. Biomes that have these conditions are the best places to grow food.
Many temperate grasslands and temperate forests have these conditions. Much of the world's grain, such as wheat and maize, is grown in these biomes.
Because the land grows crops so well, much of it has been cleared of its natural plants and changed into farmland. Few areas of these biomes are still close to their natural state.
Deserts are too dry and tundra is too cold to grow much food. Tropical rainforests are warm and wet, but their soils are often thin and low in nutrients.

a.clue: Think about what crops need to grow well.

b.q: A company wants to grow a large wheat crop. Which region would suit it best?
opts: Temperate grassland: fertile soil, steady rain, cold winters
Hot desert: sandy soil, warm all year, very little rain
Tundra: thin soil, some rain, ground frozen most of the year
Tropical rainforest: thin soil, heavy rain, warm all year
b.why: The temperate grassland has fertile soil and steady rain, and its cold winters still leave a warm enough growing season. The rainforest is tempting because it is warm and wet, but its thin, nutrient-poor soil does not suit large grain crops.
b.clue: Check each region against all three things crops need.
